reader.requirement: At --std 85 the pairing of MOVE/ADD/SUBTRACT CORRESPONDING relies on each qualifying item's name being unique once the implied qualifiers (the intermediate group names up to D1/D2) are applied, so same-named items under different qualifiers pair only with their namesake under the same qualifiers. A program whose qualifying names are not unique breaks a 'must', and 1985 requires no particular handling of that.
reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel|Edition.|IsActive|CobolVersion in CorrespondingBinder.cs: the only edition reads are perPair in Bind and the error-reporting ctx.Edition sink; CorrMatch/NamesakeCounts consult no edition.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no: 2002/2023 reword it as 'is unique' (a condition); the compiler applies the same exclusion of non-unique names at every edition, which also satisfies 1985's 'must be' because 1985 sets no requirement for a program that violates it.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: g85_bf15_03 covers same names separated by intermediate qualifiers (MOVE and ADD). Not exercised by it: a name repeated at one qualification level on the D1 side, on the D2 side, through a FILLER group, or against an ineligible (REDEFINES) twin.

probes.expected: AA pairs; CC IN S1 and CC IN S2 each pair with their namesake (unique after implied qualifiers); duplicated BB (D1), DD (D2), EE (FILLER-level twin) and FF (twin under FILLER REDEFINES) have no unique implied reference, so a conforming program cannot contain them; the compiler excludes them silently for ADD and MOVE

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.4.3 GR5  (║6.4.3 The CORRESPONDING Phrase║)  the text is in GR5
OK  §1985:I.1.6  (1.6 DEFINITION OF A CONFORMING SOURCE PROGRAM)  the text is in the clause

reader.notes: The unique-name half (qualified namesakes pair correctly) is implemented and witnessed. For a non-unique name 1985 says only 'must be unique'; 1.5.2/1.6 make that a program-conformance requirement with no detection mandate, so silently excluding the name (the later editions' reading) conforms. A diagnostic would also conform. Doubt: an adjudicator who reads 'must' as needing a compile-time refusal would record under-rejects for corr5's BB/DD/EE/FF.

refuter.evidence: rc5.cob (rc5-002) at --std 85, ADD CORRESPONDING G1 TO G2 with G1 holding FF, HH, KK once each and G2 holding each twice: printed 'R G2=100100102100103100' -- FF (twin under FILLER REDEFINES) NOT paired, HH (twin under a NAMED REDEFINES group RX) paired, KK (twin under a named ordinary subgroup SK) paired. Under 1985 qualification ('OK  §1985:IV.4.3.8.1 ... uniqueness must be established through a sequence of qualifiers which precludes any ambiguity of reference') 'FF IN G2', 'HH IN G2' and 'KK IN G2' are each equally ambiguous (1985 has no rule that a complete qualification beats a partial one), so the compiler's FILLER-versus-named distinction (NamesakeCounts counts per qualification level) is a model the 1985 text does not draw. The verdict therefore rests on a reading of GR5 ('OK  §1985:VI.6.4.3 GR5 ... must be unique after application of the implied qualifiers'): (i) uniqueness among ALL data items so named -> all three programs violate GR5, results undefined by §1985:I.1.6 ('OK  §1985:I.1.6 ... The results of violating the formats or rules of Standard COBOL are undefined'), every behaviour conforms; (ii) uniqueness among the items 'which satisfy the above conditions' (the GR4-ignored REDEFINES twins and the non-corresponding SK twin do not) -> all three programs conform and FF must pair, which the compiler does not (wrong-answer). The text does not fix the universe of 'unique'.
refuter.corrected: CONFORMS under reading (i); under reading (ii) a wrong-answer at CorrespondingBinder.cs#NamesakeCounts, which counts a FILLER-REDEFINES twin (ignored by GR4) against uniqueness while a named-REDEFINES twin is not counted.

adjudication.reason: The program's `FF`, `HH`, `KK IN G2` are ambiguous references, so it violates GR5 itself and its result is undefined. The checker rates this medium: if "unique" meant unique among the items that meet the CORRESPONDING conditions, FF would pair and the row would be a wrong answer. I take the first reading: GR5 says "each data item which satisfies the above conditions must be unique after application of the implied qualifiers", and these are not.
